Native-HD quality revision: 1920x1080 at 60 fps, high-bitrate encoding, larger labels and a compact inset HUD. Match footage is preserved at source resolution and frame rate. Tracking itself is still sampled at 3 fps. Includes a five-second introduction and eight-second result card. Supersedes the earlier 720p/12 fps draft.

Neptune Auto Scout development journal — Entry 001, recorded October 25, 2026.

Purpose: establish what the current pipeline actually understands before adding persistent robot identities. Match: 2026 FIRST in Texas District Championship, Mercury Division, Qualification 4 (2026txcmp1_qm4).

What this video shows:
- Fresh robot detection and identity tracking across three broadcast camera views.
- Green: OCR-supported team assignments. Amber: roster/motion inference. Gray: a detection without an assigned team.
- The side panel distinguishes a detected robot, a team identity, and continuity sufficient for a four-second action clip.

Measured results:
- Identity assigned at 380 of 966 sampled team-times.
- An action clip was available near 261 of 966 samples (27%). Team 6377 had none.
- The newest compatible saved local action model had zero usable action classifiers. The real prediction call emitted zero learned actions and 12 separate stationary-rule flags.
- The video exposes missed identities and non-robot detections; it is not a demonstration of accurate autonomous scouting.

Chapters:
00:00 Experiment introduction
00:13 Autonomous tracking
00:37 Teleop tracking
01:19 Assignment-change inspection interval
02:30 Late-match continuity

Method: current adopted detector and existing Apple OCR; source-bound clock/roster facts reused. CPU tracking at 3 fps; journal video at 60 fps. These availability counts are not accuracy or independent action counts. Q4 is a development match. Reserved benchmark Q7 was not used. No labels, saved corrections, released models or AWS application code were changed by this diagnostic.

Match footage: FIRST Robotics Competition broadcast. Annotations and pipeline analysis: Neptune Auto Scout.

entries.title: Neptune Journal #002 | Persistent Robot IDs: Q4 Reappearance Test | 1080p60
entries.description:
Native-HD quality revision: 1920x1080 at 60 fps, high-bitrate encoding, larger labels and a compact inset HUD. Match footage is preserved at source resolution and frame rate. Tracking itself is still sampled at 3 fps. Includes a five-second introduction and eight-second result card. Supersedes the earlier 720p/12 fps draft.

Neptune Auto Scout development journal — Entry 002, recorded October 25, 2026.

Question: can a match-level identity system retain the same robot record when an identified robot disappears and returns?

Implementation: six source-bound roster identity records, continuous tracklets, OCR-supported reconnection, camera-local appearance proposals, duplicate-identity/conflicting-read checks, and explicit unknown states during missing intervals. Reuses the exact Q4 detector observations from Journal #001. This test does not use Ollama or a newly trained robot-specific appearance network.

Actual results:
- 28 OCR-supported reconnections after gaps across all assigned camera views. This describes system evidence, not 28 independently verified correct returns.
- 26 OCR-supported returns to individual cameras and 17 camera-return proposals based on simple appearance descriptors.
- Long gaps include 5417 returning near 165s after 130s without a supported identity; 6377 returns near 106s after 63s. A robot can still be visible but unidentified during these gaps.
- The layer is conservative: supported identity availability is lower than the baseline solver. It does not yet provide reliable whole-match identity coverage.
- Existing saved human corrections were withheld from matching. 32 of 224 reference points could be assigned and agreed; 192 remained unassigned. This nonrandom development check is not a full-match accuracy benchmark.

Video overlays:
Green = OCR-supported tracklet. Amber = appearance-based proposal that needs checking. Gray = detection without an assigned persistent identity. Stable identity IDs remain in the side panel during gaps. No hidden position or action is invented. Offline analysis can use later observations.

Chapters:
00:00 Experiment introduction
00:13 Autonomous identity records
00:37 Teleop and reappearances
01:49 Team 6377 return near source 106s
02:30 Late-match identity records
02:47 Team 5417 return near source 165s

This is an engine-source prototype, not a deployed helper release. Baseline training localizations and release gates remain unchanged. There are still no usable learned action classifiers in the latest saved local model. Q4 is a development match; reserved benchmark Q7 was not used.

Baseline journal: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a7Ou42zo_Yc
Next experiment: strengthen appearance evidence and compare selective Ollama bumper-number reads on unresolved returns.

Match footage: FIRST Robotics Competition broadcast. Annotations and development analysis: Neptune Auto Scout.
